status.main_product: Blockchain-powered e-marketplace platform for buying and selling trade finance assets
status.scope_reason: The company provides a digital e-marketplace platform for financial institutions to discover, list, and trade primary and secondary trade finance assets.
status.evidence: According to Global Trade Review, the company continues to operate its blockchain-powered trade finance marketplace after mutually terminating a planned acquisition by Veefin Group in June 2025.

claims.claim: The company announced an agreement with True North Partners in May 2026 to provide member banks with access to specialized AI expertise and advisory implementation, though it hasn't specified native UCP600 or sanctions screening document checking tools.
claims.source: LinkedIn Announcement (TradeAssets and True North Partners Sign AI Enablement Agreement, May 2026)

claims.claim: Citi confirmed it joined the TradeAssets e-marketplace consortium to leverage its online, real-time portal for secondary trade asset automation alongside separate SWIFT MT798 connectivity workflows.
claims.source: Citigroup Insights: How Tech is Changing the Future of Trade

claims.claim: The platform is categorized as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) application targeting global financial institutions, having processed over $4 billion in secondary market asset distribution across its network.
claims.source: TradeAssets Website / BSE India Veefin Acquisition Corporate Filing

claims.claim: The company reports that its core secondary trade finance asset distribution e-marketplace was built using Hyperledger Fabric 1.0 blockchain technology.
claims.source: Trade Finance Global Interview / Khaleej Times

claims.claim: The company reports a growing global ecosystem of over 100 to 120 member banks across more than 35 countries using its secondary trade finance e-marketplace.
claims.source: BSE India Veefin Acquisition Corporate Filing / Globit & TradeAssets Press Release

claims.claim: Public contract announcements and partnerships verify institutional platform adoption by financial entities including YES BANK in 2018, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank (ADIB) and British Arab Commercial Bank (BACB) in 2019, United Arab Bank (UAB) in 2020, and Banco Latinoamericano de Comercio Exterior (Bladex) in 2022.
claims.source: Zawya Press Release (Sept 24, 2018); Cash & Trade Magazine (May 29, 2019); British Arab Commercial Bank News (April 30, 2021); United Arab Bank Media Center (Jan 27, 2020); Bladex Official Announcement (Nov 21, 2022).

claims.claim: The company announced senior placements across different regions in 2019, including hiring an executive director for South and Central Asia based in Singapore and business development and executive directors based in London.
claims.source: Global Trade Review (Feb 13, 2020) - 'TradeAssets makes string of new hires across globe'.

claims.claim: The planned acquisition of TradeAssets by Estorifi Solutions (a Veefin Group company), which was announced in February 2025, was mutually and amicably terminated in June 2025 because the transaction extended beyond the agreed timeline.
claims.corrected: The planned acquisition of TradeAssets by Estorifi Solutions (a Veefin Group company), which was announced in February 2025, was mutually and amicably terminated in June 2025 because the transaction extended beyond the agreed timeline due to evolving strategic directions.
claims.source: Global Trade Review (June 25, 2025) - 'Veefin and TradeAssets end acquisition talks'.

claims.claim: TradeAssets reports that its digital trade finance e-marketplace operates across more than 35 countries and has processed over $3.5 billion in transaction volume.
claims.source: TradeAssets Official Website Product Overview Page (tradeassets.online).

claims.claim: The platform grew its network to nearly 80 member banks by late 2021, establishing active corridor participations with institutions like Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank and Citibank.
claims.note: The total network size reaching nearly 80 member banks by late 2021 and an active corridor participation with Citibank could not be verified in published sources.
claims.source: Global Trade Review event agendas and news archives.
